## Purpose and timing

After the current demonstration and stable experimental-baseline checkpoint (#9), run a **small separate prototype with a few hand-authored study activities**. Use findings to refine the specification before committing a production study-method system. This is a discovery experiment under #14, not adoption of a planner/interface or a prerequisite for the current recording/merge review.

## Authored inputs and uncertainty

Each fictional activity supplies a topic, illustrative procedure/method, estimated duration and required resources/context. Keep the first examples simple enough to isolate representation and placement; methods and durations are authored test assumptions, not proven optima.

Unknown energy, location and resources stay unknown. Use selective consequential questions and explicit provisional assumptions. A workday is not proof of tiredness. Optional self-report may inform a user choice without becoming a health/capacity inference. Load preferences are provisional for the current horizon, rechecked when needed.

## Acceptance for the experiment

- [ ] Prepare a small inspectable activity inventory tied to the selected synthetic course materials, with known facts, authored assumptions and unknowns clearly separated.
- [ ] Compare a baseline and paired cases changing one fact at a time: e.g. a required resource unavailable, an explicit load preference, or missing optional context. State the expected observable behavior before running.
- [ ] Verify relevant answers affect a structured, reviewable proposal; resource conflicts are avoided or surfaced; unknowns do not become invented facts; the user can correct assumptions.
- [ ] Keep task, method, course allocation and placement distinguishable. Do not evaluate learning effectiveness through scheduled/completed minutes or pleasant explanations.
- [ ] Record deterministic feasibility checks separately from agent/human judgments of usefulness, question burden and explanation accuracy. Preserve failures and configuration; reuse authorized models only.
- [ ] Present examples/results and identify what should change in the spec, remain unknown or be deferred. Obtain the existing foundation selections before expanding a selected implementation into the full workflow.

Later work may explore approved guidance, method selection/spacing, optional feedback, preference revision, context compatibility and retention outcomes. Those need their own evidence and decisions. No real-calendar/workspace pilot, automatic medical inference, broad method catalog or fully personalized learning engine is included here.

## Purpose and timing

After the current demonstration and bounded baseline readiness/integration checkpoint (#9), investigate a small scheduling-quality improvement before expanding to study-method personalization. This is a bounded experiment on the existing heuristic, not a solver selection or the full #14 architecture. It is not silently added as a blanket #8 merge requirement; any current-demo blocker must have an explicit readiness disposition.

## Agreed review expectations

- With matching deadlines and unknown mastery/remaining work, aim for roughly equal time **across the horizon**, allowing weekly variation.
- Balance is a **soft default**. Explain justified departures for known workload, urgency, availability or explicit priority. Equal time is not evidence of equal learning need.
- Ask one consequential workday/weekend tradeoff question when the answer could materially change the proposal.
- Treat the load choice as provisional for the current horizon; recheck at checkpoints/material changes. Missing energy/place/resource context stays unknown.

## Measured problem

Both current Luna API attempts produced 19h Algoritmos / 11h Banco de Dados across six weeks, then 18h/12h after the Monday correction, with no known need justifying the skew. The agent asked course priority but did not ask about workday/weekend concentration. Revised week: Wednesday 2h, Saturday 2h, Sunday 1h. [Evidence and explanations](https://github.com/Residencia-em-IA-Challenge-2-Grupo-12/DSH-Prototype/blob/fb89772/docs/onboarding/luna-schedule-review.md).

The current tool supports hours, weeks, date exclusions, period and course focus. It has no explicit horizon-balance objective or workday/weekend load input. Do not encode a soft preference as an absolute date ban or promise that a prompt change alone implements it.

## Bounded acceptance

- [ ] Write a small paired scenario set before freezing the detailed contract; keep calendar/context constant and vary only balance/explicit priority/load choice per comparison.
- [ ] Report per-course hours over the horizon, weekly load and constraint violations independently of the agent's prose. Show whether the proposed baseline default removes arbitrary ordering bias in the equal-deadline case.
- [ ] Cover explicit priority, unequal/expired deadlines, unavailable capacity, Monday correction, daily limits/breaks and preserved existing events. A soft preference must allow explained fallback or shortfall rather than hidden constraint changes.
- [ ] Choose the narrowest provisional representation for load preference after examples are inspected; make scope and provenance visible. Retain the later heuristic/CP-SAT selection checkpoint.
- [ ] Verify that a consequential answer changes supported planner inputs and/or a reviewable result, and that the explanation matches actual allocation. Avoid repetitive questions about available facts.
- [ ] Demonstrate rejection/stale approval still prevents writes after revision. Keep simulator-only, separate near/future approval and immutable review semantics.
- [ ] Present findings and limits before adopting broader task/method/context behavior. No learned fatigue scores, automatic retention claims or general workspace execution.

Parent area: #14; related #4, #13. The authored-activity prototype is a separate later exploration.


## Current next action — organization handoff

Remain Backlog behind #9. Inspect paired examples before freezing a new load-preference contract; ownership is not assigned yet.
